div.p: The aim is to achieve schedulability of tasks in a real time system with fault tolerance and energy minimization. The fault tolerance can be achieved by maintaining enough time redundancy so that task can be re-executed in presence of fault. During re-execution, checkpointing policy gives reliability in a system. First, calculate an optimal number of checkpoints to reduce the redundancy and save the system to complete re-execution. Energy minimization can be achieved by DVFS (Dynamic Voltage Frequency & Scaling). In this paper, existing non-preemptive EDF scheduling algorithm has been modified for fault tolerance and energy minimization. We adjust the voltage level according to available storage energy in the system & find feasibility test on each task. The worst case execution time is associated with voltage level. The approach is developed to enhance task schedulability and minimize energy consumption in presence of fault. At the end of the paper, experimental results shows that proposed algorithm is better than existing algorithm.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Real time systems are used to generate logically correct result at their relative deadline. Modern real time systems have reliability with minimum energy consumption. Reliability depends upon number of tasks completed within its relative deadline [1], [8]. Without any failure in the system and to achieve continuous reliability, authors are usually worked on fault tolerance with minimum energy consumption system [5]. A system may fail due to fault in a system with available sufficient energy. Transient fault is more frequent than permanent fault. This fault cannot easily be appear or detected during re-execution without appearance of fault we could not find reliability in a system then considering fault tolerance techniques are used for tolerating at most a single transient fault during execution [13] [14]. To overcome transient fault problem in real time systems, we should use the most common time redundancy fault tolerance techniques-re-execution, checkpointing and rollback. Re execution means re-execution of faulty task but such that fault visible for same time then sudden disappears. Next common or effective fault tolerant technique is checkpointing. It is that technique which is first necessary state of the system to be saved onto CPU. Before saving the necessary state, it is stored on CPU. First check acts as an acceptance test on the possible occurrence of transient faults in a system. Then, calculate sufficient or an optimal number of checkpoints for fault recovery in the system. Real time systems need same source of energy to do any job [5]. Consider two techniques to minimize energy consumption in the system. First is DVFS & second is DPD. DVFS is dynamic voltage frequency scaling technique. DVFS is assigned a voltage level that is adjusted according to available storage energy in the system [1] [9]. A Real time system has storage energy depending upon the capacity of the system. Sometimes it may be chargeable and sometimes not. It totally depends upon the system needs. DVFS is a policy to manage energy in the system [2] [6]. During execution, each task is assigned a voltage level and adjusting that voltage to minimize energy consumption in the system. The energy consumption of each task is depending upon voltage and frequency such that, if P is the power required for a system and V and f is frequency of a task respectively then ܲ ‫ן‬ ܸ ଶ ݂ Using above equation, the energy consumption can be minimized by adjusting voltage and frequency of a system. If voltage or frequency a system is reduced then total power consumption is also reduced. In this paper the EDF scheduling algorithm has been modified such that the fault tolerance is achieved with minimum power consumption. We apply checkpointing approach for fault tolerance and DVS for reducing energy consumption. We combine both the approaches to achieve fault tolerance with minimum energy consumption.

Rest of the paper is organized as follows. The literature survey is presented in section II. In section III basic terms and problem description has been explained. The proposed algorithm is presented in section IV. Section V shows the results and analysis of this paper. Finally section VI concludes the paper.

div.head: II. LITERATURE SURVEY
div.p: Several approaches have been proposed for fault tolerance with energy minimization. Most of the approaches are based on checkpointing to tolerate transient fault. The major consideration is to adjust the intervals between checkpoints to reduce energy consumption. The deadline of task is also the major factor in real time system. Checkpointing and rollback recovery are used to improve the reliability and availability of fault-tolerant computing systems [3][4] [7]. These approaches have been an active area of research in real time scenario. Most of the researchers are working on energy minimization and enhancing schedulability of task [10]. The main problem of checkpointing is how to determine strategies for optimal placement of checkpoints. The performance of the system is depends upon placement of checkpoint. The system will be more efficient with fault tolerance if an optimal number of checkpoints have been applied.

The number of checkpoints affects the execution time, task response time and expected cost. Some researchers have tackled the problem of checkpoint placement within the framework of probabilistic optimization.

Researchers are also working for reducing energy consumption using DVS. As DVS is based on dynamic voltage scaling and its corresponding frequency scaling approach, the researchers try to combine this approach with fault tolerance.

Earliest Deadline First (EDF) [10] scheduling approach has been used for past many years to schedule real time tasks in various time critical applications. However, EDF does not provide mechanisms for managing time redundancy and fault tolerance [7][8], so that real-time tasks will finish their execution within deadlines even in the presence of faults. In this paper, EDF is modified such that tasks complete the execution in the presence of fault within its deadline.

div.head: III. BASIC TERMS AND PROBLEM DESCRIPTION
A. Task Model
div.p: Consider a set T of n independent aperiodic tasks where T = {T 1 , T 2 …… T n } where T i = (a i, c i , d i ). It can be represented as a i = arrival time of the task, c i = computation time of the task & d i = deadline of the task in a system. Each task t i is associated with voltage level V i as well as frequency f i . In this paper, we consider initially each task is running on maximum voltage and frequency level. Each task is released on its arrival time with execution/computation time and deadline. It is assumed that tasks are arranged in a non-decreasing order. When the new task arrives, it is scheduled as early as possible. If there is no another task available, we check the available slack time and adjust the voltage level to reduce energy consumption [12]. If another task has been arrived with relatively large deadline then we also reduce the voltage level to schedule the task and minimize energy consumption. We designed a non-preemptive EDF scheduling with fault tolerance & minimized energy consumption on modifying voltage levels associated to each task according to available storage energy in the system and slack time. A voltage level is directly proportional to the energy of the system. If there is a decrease in level of voltage, then corresponding energy also decreases in the system. This method is known as dynamic voltage frequency scaling in real time system. Each task is scheduled by EDF scheduling algorithm. If a new task has the higher priority & the processor is busy scheduling any other task then the processor will not preempted to higher priority task & lower priority task will continue to finish its execution [11] [13].

div.head: B. Energy management Specification
div.p: In this paper, it is assumed that consumption energy can vary according to modified voltage in a system. Energy storage is recharged & it depends upon the capacity of the system [4] [5]. When a task is executed in a system, it drains same energy from the system. If storage energy is enough for task execution, then the task easily executes otherwise it is discarded.
